lines.trans: It is almost noon! Let us ask Mazen if any packages arrived.
Welcome back! Did you find treasure, or just three tired pairs of feet?
We are missing one final piece, Mazen. Look closely at the front desk.
Wait, look at the corner of the guest register... under the brass pen!
A small square of watercolour paper! Hand it here quickly!
The postman left that an hour ago; there is no return address.
It matches the other three perfectly. We have all four corners now.
What does the back of this fourth piece say?
Nothing! It is completely blank except for a faint blue line.
How does a blank piece of paper help us open the small sealed envelope?
Bring all four corners together... hand me Cards One, Two, and Three, Nour!

Goodbye!

meanings.note: Placed directly before an indefinite noun without ال- to mean 'the last' (آخر يوم 'the last day', آخر الساحة 'the far end of the courtyard').

examples.trans: The attic room is at the end of the floor.
Today is the last day of the week.

meanings.note: The number four, used with masculine nouns.

examples.trans: I bought four books.
The guests arrived at four in the afternoon.

meanings.note: The color blue.

examples.trans: The color of my car is blue.

examples.text: السما اليوم لونها أزرق صافي وما في غيم.
examples.trans: The sky today is a clear blue and there are no clouds.

meanings.note: Relational adjective from أمام ('in front of'): الغرفة الأمامية / الباب الأمامي.

examples.text: علقنا اللوحة الجديدة جنب البوابة الأمامية.
examples.trans: We hung the new sign beside the front gate.
The front windows look straight out onto the lane.

meanings.note: Warm greeting used alone (أهلا!), with فيك/فيكي ('welcome to you!'), or paired as أهلا وسهلا! ('you are most welcome!').

examples.trans: Hello, I am Tariq!
Welcome to Jasmine House!

meanings.note: Used as a question word or indefinite pronoun.

examples.trans: Which car do you prefer?

examples.text: بأي ساعة رح يبلش الاجتماع اليوم؟
examples.trans: At what hour is the meeting going to start today?

meanings.note: Everyday conditional word 'if' for real possibilities.

examples.text: رني الجرس إذا احتجتي أي شي.
examples.trans: Ring the bell if you need anything.

examples.text: إذا فتحنا الساحة الصبح، الجيران بيفرحوا.
examples.trans: If we open the courtyard in the morning, the neighbours will be delighted.

meanings.note: The typical Jordanian form of شي: في إشي؟ 'is something wrong?', ولا إشي 'nothing at all'.

examples.text: في إشي بدك إياه من السوق؟
examples.trans: Is there anything you want from the market?
Nothing happened at all, relax.

meanings.note: Appears in everyday speech inside warm set phrases such as إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again!').

examples.trans: See you soon, sir!
Goodbye and until next time.

meanings.note: The number two. Often pronounced 'tnēn' in Jordanian.

examples.trans: I have two children.

examples.text: طلبنا فنجانين قهوة وكاستين شاي للاثنين.
examples.trans: We ordered two cups of coffee and two glasses of tea for the two of us.

meanings.note: Command to a male to wait.

examples.trans: Wait just a minute.

examples.text: استنى شوي، أنا نازل معك هسه!
examples.trans: Wait a second—I'm coming down with you right now!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: A postcard arrived in the morning.
The postman rang the bell.

meanings.note: Extremely common Jordanian word meaning both 'only / just' (بس نص كاسة 'just half a glass') and 'but' between clauses.

examples.text: بدي أقرأ الدفتر، بس مش ملاقي نظارتي!
examples.trans: I want to read the ledger, only I cannot find my glasses!
Just half a glass, please.

meanings.note: After a plural verb, بعض means 'each other' (بننادي بعض 'we call each other').

examples.trans: We call each other by first name here.

examples.text: ما حكينا مع بعض من زمان.
examples.trans: We have not spoken with each other in a long time.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: تانية, plural: تانيين).

examples.trans: Room four is on the second floor.
There is a second sheet behind the letter.

meanings.note: Indicates physical location beneath something.

examples.trans: The cat is hiding under the table.

examples.text: لقينا البطاقة التانية تحت الصحن الأبيض.
examples.trans: We found the second card under the white plate.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بترك, بيترك).

examples.text: مين ترك هاد المغلف جنب الجرس؟
examples.trans: Who left this envelope by the bell?
Thank you for not leaving me in the rain.

meanings.note: Universal everyday Jordanian adjective for 'tired' (feminine: تعبانة, plural: تعبانين).

examples.text: أنا تعبان شوي من رحلة الباص الطويلة.
examples.trans: I am a little tired from the long bus trip.

examples.text: صوتي تعبان اليوم، بس قلبي فرحان.
examples.trans: My voice is tired today, but my heart is glad.

meanings.note: Adverbial accusative of تقريب (approximation).

examples.text: صارت الساعة الضهر تقريبا، خلينا نرتاح.
examples.trans: It is almost noon now, let us take a rest.

examples.text: الكيكة جاهزة تقريبا، ضايل لها خمس دقايق.
examples.trans: The cake is almost ready; five minutes are left.

meanings.note: The number 3 when followed by a counted noun.

examples.trans: I have three cars in the garage.

examples.text: مشينا تلات دقايق وبعدين وصلنا عالبوابة.
examples.trans: We walked three minutes and then reached the gate.

meanings.note: The standalone form of the number 3.

examples.trans: Count to ten: one, two, three.

examples.text: رتبنا الصحون واحد تنين تلاتة عالطاولة.
examples.trans: We lined up the plates one, two, three on the table.

meanings.note: Used to emphasize absolute completion or exactness.

examples.trans: I agree with you completely.

examples.text: النتيجة طلعت متل ما توقعنا تماما.
examples.trans: The result turned out exactly as we expected.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بجمع, بيجمع).

examples.trans: Today our courtyard brings a family together!
We gathered the chairs under the tree.

meanings.note: Collective noun for walnuts; خشب جوز is walnut wood. (Not to be confused with جوز 'husband; pair', a different everyday sense.)

examples.trans: I bought a kilo of walnuts at the market.
The cake has walnuts and honey in it.

meanings.note: Can mean a physical line, a phone line, a bus route, or handwriting.

examples.trans: There is no coverage, the line is disconnecting.

examples.text: رسمنا خط مستقيم بالمسطرة على الورقة.
examples.trans: We drew a straight line with the ruler on the sheet.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: خفيفة, plural: خفاف).

examples.trans: Coffee with milk and light sugar.
A light, tasty breakfast in the morning.

meanings.note: Imperative forms with object pronouns give خليكم بحالكم ('stay in your own business') and خلوني بحالي ('leave me in mine').

examples.trans: Let me speak for a bit.
Stay calm, Mariam.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: دفاتر.

examples.trans: We wrote the name in the booking ledger.
I forgot my leather notebook on the table.

meanings.note: Ordinal number from أربعة (four). Feminine: رابعة.

examples.text: البند الرابع عشر من قانون عمان القديمة.
examples.trans: Clause fourteen of the Amman Old Quarter Act.
This is the fourth cup of coffee today.

meanings.note: Instance noun (ism marra) from رجع ('return').

examples.text: قطار الرجعة بيطلع من المحطة الساعة سبعة.
examples.trans: The return train leaves the station at seven o'clock.

examples.text: بطريق الرجعة من السوق، اشترينا نعنع أخضر.
examples.trans: On the way back from the market, we bought fresh green mint.

meanings.note: Feminine body-part noun in Levantine Arabic (رجلك اليمين 'your right foot').

examples.text: ارفعي رجلك عالمخدة وارتاحي نص ساعة.
examples.trans: Prop your foot up on the pillow and rest for half an hour.

examples.text: حطيت كيس تلج ملفوف بمنشفة على رجلي.
examples.trans: I placed an ice pack wrapped in a towel on my foot.

meanings.note: Future tense marker in Jordanian and Levantine Arabic, equivalent to 'sa-' in MSA.

examples.trans: I will travel tomorrow.

examples.text: رح نذوق التلات كيكات بعد ما يبردوا شوي.
examples.trans: We will taste the three cakes after they cool a little.

meanings.note: Refers to a corner of a room or street, or a geometric angle.

examples.trans: Put the chair in the corner.
The chest is placed in the northern corner of the room.

meanings.note: Used almost universally in the Levantine adverbial phrase بالزبط (biz-zabt, 'exactly / right on').

examples.text: هاد هو اللون الأخضر اللي بدنا إياه بالزبط!
examples.trans: That is the exact shade of green we want!

examples.text: وصل السايق عالباب الساعة تنتين بالزبط.
examples.trans: The driver arrived at the gate at two o'clock sharp.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بسأل, بيسأل).

examples.trans: Ask him what his name is on the phone!
I came down to ask about the sink water.

meanings.note: Everyday word for an hour of time, a wristwatch, or a wall clock.

examples.trans: I've been waiting for you for an hour.

examples.text: المكتبة بتفتح كمان ساعة، خلينا نستنى بالحديقة.
examples.trans: The library opens in another hour; let us wait in the garden.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بساعد, بيساعد).

examples.trans: He will surely love to help us!
We helped the guest carry her suitcase.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun; ساعي البريد means 'postman / courier'. Plural: سعاة.

examples.trans: The postman brought a thick envelope.
I handed the signature to the mail carrier.

meanings.note: With ب- forms the very common adverb بسرعة ('quickly / fast').

examples.trans: I always walk fast in the morning.
Your quick wit saved the day!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian interrogative pronoun for 'what'.

examples.trans: What are you doing here?

examples.text: شو المكون السري اللي ضفتيه عالعجينة؟
examples.trans: What is the secret ingredient that you added to the batter?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بصير, بيصير).

examples.trans: You became one of us quickly!
Did the water upstairs turn cold?

meanings.note: Adjective used for size (small) or age (young), masculine singular.

examples.text: عندي أخ صغير عمره خمس سنين.
examples.trans: I have a young brother who is five years old.

examples.text: في مفتاح نحاس صغير مخبي تحت الورقة.
examples.trans: There is a small brass key hidden under the sheet.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian spelling/pronunciation (duhur) for midday (12:00 p.m.).

examples.text: الكافيه بيقدم شوربة سخنة من الضهر للمسا.
examples.trans: The café serves hot soup from noon until evening.

examples.text: الشمس بتكون عالية ودافية وقت الضهر.
examples.trans: The sun is high and warm at noon.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun (feminine: ضيفة). Plural: ضيوف.

examples.trans: The guests are coming down to breakfast now.
We welcomed every guest with a smile.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: طوابق.

examples.trans: Your room is on the second floor on the right.
The building has three storeys.

meanings.note: Used for mailed parcels and wrapped packages; plural طرود.

examples.text: وصل طرد مربوط بخيط قنب للمكتبة.
examples.trans: A parcel tied with hemp string arrived at the library.

examples.text: فتحنا الطرد الصغير ولقينا جواته خريطة.
examples.trans: We opened the small package and found a map inside.

meanings.note: Pronounced duhur in everyday Jordanian: الظهر means 'at noon / midday'.

examples.trans: He will arrive Friday at noon.
The sun is high at midday.

meanings.note: Exception preposition often preceded by ما (ما عدا) in both formal and colloquial Jordanian.

examples.text: كل الكيكات بردت عدا صينية وحدة بالفرن.
examples.trans: All the cakes have cooled except one tin in the oven.

examples.text: الكل وصل عالوقت ما عدا رامي.
examples.trans: Everyone arrived on time apart from Rami.

meanings.note: Standard preposition for 'on', 'upon', or 'to'.

examples.trans: The book is on the table.

examples.text: حطينا الخريطة على الطاولة وبلشنا نحللها.
examples.trans: We laid the map on the table and began analysing it.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: عناوين.

examples.text: خد رقم النزل وعنواننا لو سمحت.
examples.trans: Take the guesthouse number and our address, please.
The address is written clearly on the card.

meanings.note: Used to describe an empty container or a person who has free time.

examples.trans: I am free today in the afternoon.

examples.text: الرف الفوقاني فاضي، بنقدر نحط العلبة عليه.
examples.trans: The top shelf is empty; we can put the tin on it.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بفتح, بيفتح).

examples.trans: The corner shop opens at seven.
Oh, the door finally opened!

meanings.note: Preposition for 'in' or 'at', and very commonly used to mean 'there is/are' (existential).

examples.trans: There are many people in the market.

examples.text: في تلات بطاقات ملونة جوا الظرف الكبير.
examples.trans: There are three coloured cards inside the big envelope.

meanings.note: Preposition and adverb for time or sequence meaning 'prior to' or 'before'.

examples.trans: I have to arrive before five o'clock.

examples.text: غسلنا الفواكه منيح قبل ما نقطعها للتذوق.
examples.trans: We washed the fruit thoroughly before slicing it for the tasting.

meanings.note: Used to count items, or mean a portion, slice, or spare part.

examples.trans: I want a piece of cake please.

examples.text: كل واحد فينا أخذ قطعة صغيرة من كيكة اللوز.
examples.trans: Each one of us took a small piece of the almond cake.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun; قلم رصاص means 'pencil'. Plural: أقلام.

examples.trans: I found my pen in the jacket pocket.
We write the names with a pencil.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun; كرت بريد means 'postcard'. Plural: كروت.

examples.text: بعتتله كرت بريد قصير الأسبوع الماضي.
examples.trans: I sent him a short postcard last week.
I recognised his neat handwriting on the card right away.

meanings.note: Refers to a literal treasure or something highly valued metaphorically.

examples.trans: They found an old treasure underground.

examples.text: الوصفات السرية اللي بالدفتر أغلى من أي كنز.
examples.trans: The secret recipes in the notebook are more precious than any treasure.

meanings.note: The main interrogative word for asking about manner or state.

examples.trans: How are you today?

examples.text: كيف قدرت تفتح القفل القديم بدون ما تكسره؟
examples.trans: How did you manage to open the old lock without breaking it?

meanings.note: Core word in إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again / goodbye!') and also 'reunion / meeting'.

examples.trans: Goodbye, have a pleasant trip!

examples.text: كان لقاء دافي بعد غياب طويل.
examples.trans: It was a warm reunion after a long absence.

meanings.note: Form I defective verb (fa'il class: لقي / يلقى) used extensively in Jordanian speech for finding lost objects.

examples.text: لقينا ثلاث بطاقات قديمة جوا الكتاب.
examples.trans: We found three old cards inside the book.

examples.text: مازن لقي الوصفة الأصلية بخط جدته.
examples.trans: Mazen found the original recipe in his grandmother's handwriting.

لهون.gloss: here; hither; up to this point

meanings.en: here; hither; up to this point
meanings.note: Combines لـ (to, toward) with هون (here); used for motion toward the speaker or stopping at a limit.

examples.text: تعال لهون يا طارق عشان تشوف الرسمة.
examples.trans: Come over here, Tariq, so you can see the drawing.

examples.text: لهون وبس، خلصنا حل اللغز بنجاح!
examples.trans: Up to here and no further—we have solved the puzzle successfully!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ألوان.

examples.trans: The colour of the suitcase is dark blue.
The courtyard colours are soothing to the eye.

meanings.note: Used mostly as a negative particle for verbs ('didn't') or as a relative pronoun/conjunction ('what' or 'that which').

examples.trans: I haven't eaten anything since the morning.

examples.text: ما عرفت إنه العلبة فيها طابق سري من تحت.
examples.trans: I did not know that the box had a secret compartment underneath.

meanings.note: Relates to water, used for colors (light blue/watery), animals, or parks (e.g. water park).

examples.trans: We went to an aquatic amusement park (water park).

examples.text: استعمل الرسام لون مائي أزرق عشان يرسم البحر.
examples.trans: The painter used a blue watercolour to paint the sea.

meanings.note: Passive participle of ختم (to stamp/seal), modifying مغلف in definiteness and gender.

examples.text: وصل مغلّف مختوم من البلدية اليوم الصبح.
examples.trans: A stamped envelope from the municipality arrived this morning.

examples.text: لازم الورقة تكون مختومة بختم رسمي عشان يقبلوها.
examples.trans: The paper has to be stamped with an official seal for them to accept it.

meanings.note: Denotes a square shape or a square area in geometry or real-world objects.

examples.trans: Draw a square on the paper.

examples.text: رسمنا مربع صغير جنب كل رقم عالورقة.
examples.trans: We drew a small square next to each number on the sheet.

meanings.note: Form IV active participle of أرسل used substantively for the sender named on a letter or parcel.

examples.text: اسم المرسل مكتوب على ظهر المغلف بالحبر الأسود.
examples.trans: The sender's name is written on the back of the envelope in black ink.

examples.text: وصلنا الطرد بس ما عرفنا مين المرسل.
examples.trans: We received the parcel, but we did not know who the sender was.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'with'; takes pronoun suffixes to express 'have on one's person' (معي 'I have with me', معك حق 'you are right').

examples.trans: You are right, Nour!
Goodbye! (lit. go with safety)

meanings.note: Refers to a paper envelope used for letters or documents.

examples.trans: I put the money in an envelope.

examples.text: حطينا البطاقات كلها جوا مغلف ورق بني.
examples.trans: We put all the cards inside a brown paper envelope.

meanings.note: Used for both a workplace (office) and the piece of furniture (desk).

examples.trans: I am waiting for you in my office.

examples.text: لقينا الخريطة التانية جوا درج مكتب جدي.
examples.trans: We found the second map inside my grandfather's desk drawer.

meanings.note: Often used as a noun meaning 'letter' (mail) or 'destiny' in traditional contexts.

examples.trans: The name is written on the board.

examples.text: الرقم مكتوب بخط صغير تحت الختم الأحمر.
examples.trans: The number is written in small handwriting beneath the red seal.

meanings.note: One of the most basic Arabic prepositions indicating origin.

examples.trans: I am from Jordan.

examples.text: جبنا العسل البلدي الصافي من مزرعة قريبة.
examples.trans: We brought the pure local honey from a nearby farm.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'good' and adverbially 'well' (نمت منيح؟ 'did you sleep well?').

examples.trans: It has a good, comfortable wooden bed.
Did you sleep well under the wooden ceiling?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: ناقصة, plural: ناقصين).

examples.trans: Tell me what is missing in the room?

examples.text: الأغراض كاملة ما فيها شي ناقص.
examples.trans: Everything is complete with nothing missing.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بناول, بيناول).

examples.trans: Hand me the heavy iron wrench.
Pass me the teacup, please.

meanings.note: Used for the metal or objects made of it.

examples.trans: This jug is made of copper.

examples.text: الإبريق والمصفاية معمولين من نحاس مطروق قديم.
examples.trans: The teapot and strainer are made of old hammered copper.

meanings.note: Imperative-only verb in everyday Arabic, inflected for gender and number: هات (to a man), هاتي (to a woman), هاتوا (plural).

examples.text: هات السلة التقيلة عنك يا أستاذ مازن.
examples.trans: Give me that heavy basket for you, Mr Mazen.

examples.text: هاتي القلم الرصاص من على المكتب يا نور.
examples.trans: Hand me the pencil from the desk, Nour.

meanings.note: Signature urban Jordanian/Levantine adverb for now (also spelled هلا in Jordan).

examples.text: هلق رح نفتح الصينية ونذوق أول قطعة.
examples.trans: Right now we will open the tin and taste the first piece.
We finished writing the notes just now.

meanings.note: Cardinal number or used as an indefinite pronoun.

examples.trans: There is someone asking about you.

examples.text: اشتريت كتاب واحد بس من المعرض لأنه كان غالي.
examples.trans: I bought just one book from the fair because it was expensive.

meanings.note: Collective noun used for paper material or leaves of a tree.

examples.text: جيب لي شوية ورق أكتب عليهم.
examples.trans: Bring me some paper to write on.

examples.text: لفينا ورق دوالي اليوم الصبح للغدا مع اللبن.
examples.trans: We rolled grape leaves this morning for lunch with yogurt.

meanings.note: One sheet of paper or one leaf; the collective ورق means paper in general.

examples.trans: Write your number down for me on a piece of paper.
The tree leaf turns yellow in autumn.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بوصل, بيوصل).

examples.trans: Our guest arrived right on the second!
An official letter arrived at noon.

meanings.note: Used in negative constructions or as a strong negative emphasis.

examples.trans: Not even one of them came.

examples.text: سألت الكل بس ولا حدا بيعرف وين حطوا المفتاح.
examples.trans: I asked everyone, yet not a single person knows where they put the key.

meanings.note: Vocative particle used when addressing someone directly.

examples.trans: Oh Ahmed, come here.

examples.text: يا سيدي، تفضل اشرب معنا فنجان قهوة قبل ما تروح.
examples.trans: Sir, please come have a cup of coffee with us before you leave.
